title: Preppers
victoryHeadline: Prepared for everything except getting caught
acts: The Bunkerbrook household had drilled for eleven kinds of apocalypse and never once rehearsed an ordinary Tuesday. Out on the grass, Vivianna crouched by the shrubs with her clipboard, cross-checking the boxes stacked under the old porch TV against her master list, three tins short of closing out the quarter's audit. Up the slope, Angelo spent the afternoon stacking crates onto the roof rack of the bug-out car, working out loud how many tins the axle would tolerate before the suspension gave, and complaining that the slope out front made the handbrake next to useless. The one box he left strictly alone was the one wedged against the shed door, which was a job for the weekend. Upstairs, Carolina stood at the bedroom shelf with her clipboard, running the tinned-goods count for the third time, because the number kept coming out three hundred and ninety short of what the ledger said should be there. Behind her, flat on the bed with his boots still on, Blake called it 'rest-cycle conditioning' and refused, on principle, to specify what he was conditioning for.

Down in the safe room, Daryl lay on the bunk with a stopwatch, timing how long she could go without checking whether anyone had noticed she was scared of the dark down here, and getting a little further each time. At the far shelf, Edna knelt quietly re-sorting the entire tinned-goods wall into alphabetical order — a habit she'd never told anyone about, and one that was, this particular afternoon, about to make Carolina's count come out very strange indeed. In the kitchen, alone at the table under his enormous hat, Greg worked his way through a fifteen-year-old pouch of freeze-dried stroganoff one determined spoonful at a time, narrating each mouthful like a man filing an incident report. Across the hall, Howie sat guarding a bathtub he'd filled to the brim with drinking water, in a chair he'd carried in specially, watching a small television he didn't trust an inch.

It was Friedrich who first noticed something, and only because the broadcast finally ended. He had stood three feet from the living-room TV through the entire emergency test, taking notes of his own and not once glancing at the window — which was exactly why nobody in the house had clocked the low, patient rumble outside forty minutes earlier, or the long screech of shrubbery, or the horn that played eight cheerful notes nobody could name. By the time he looked up, the yard had gone very quiet and had acquired a car-shaped gap in the hedge. The tin mystery solved itself before the bigger one did: Edna's reorganised shelf had simply put the beans somewhere Carolina hadn't thought to check, and Blake, cornered, admitted to a certain amount of midnight snacking that explained a much smaller shortfall than anyone had feared. It explained nothing at all about the yard.

reveal: It was Angelo, in the Yard, with the bug-out car. The mismatched tin count wasn't food going missing at all — it was food he'd quietly diverted for himself over a long, lean winter while insisting on tighter rations for everyone else, and Vivianna's audit was three days from proving it down to the last stolen tin. So he finished loading the car exactly as heavy as he needed it, walked round to the driver's side, and let the handbrake go on the slope he'd spent the whole afternoon complaining about, then stepped well clear as several hundred kilos of tinned peaches rolled downhill into the one spot in the yard where Vivianna, clipboard in hand, was counting boxes with her back to the house. He was three fields away restacking supplies by the time anyone thought to ask where the car had got to.

escape.generic: The case went cold, the household doubled down on inventory audits out of sheer spite, and the one person who'd actually done it kept right on prepping, rations intact, conscience apparently unaffected.

byAccused.B: Blake was hauled off still calling it rest-cycle conditioning, and got in one last rep of lying very still in the back of the car before anyone stopped him.
byAccused.C: Carolina's only comment, all the way out, was that the actual count was still three hundred and ninety tins short and somebody really ought to look into that.
byAccused.D: Daryl's stopwatch was still running when she was led away, and nobody ever did find out what her personal best would have been.
byAccused.E: Edna's shelf stayed alphabetised for exactly one more day before Carolina, in a fit of grief-stricken tidying, put everything back the wrong way round.
byAccused.F: Friedrich never did work out what all the fuss outside had been about, and to this day maintains it must have been in the broadcast, which he watched twice more just to be sure.
byAccused.G: Greg was walked out of the kitchen mid-spoonful, stroganoff pouch and all, on the theory that if it hadn't killed him yet, evidence tampering wasn't out of the question.
byAccused.H: Howie's bathtub, deprived of its guard, was quietly drained by someone doing the dishes three days later, and nobody ever mentioned it again.
